- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from 18-day mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline after peak at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.27 or higher) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves in 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative — add 2–4% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 18-day window — if 30d forecast is >15% above 18d mean, adjust down by 5–8% to reflect momentum decay.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit recent volatility — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before final output.
